text.p: Norwegian offshore services company Petroleum Geo-Services ASA (PGS) said on Wedneday it had record earnings in 1996 and had completed its first five years in business as a leader in the marine seismic industry.

The company, which has headquarters in Oslo, Norway and Houston in Texas in the United States, booked a 57 percent jump in operating profits to $91 million against $58 million in 1995. Profits before tax rose almost 40 percent to $72 million compared with $52 million.
Fourth-quarter operating and pre-tax profits of $20 million and $16 million respectively also were higher than ever before.
"PGS continued its growth trend by achieving record revenues and earnings for the fourth quarter of 1996," a statement said.

"During this five year inaugural period...Very little of the company's growth has been achieved through acquisitions but rather through a well-executed five-year plan that addressed the oil industry's desire to obtain 3D seismic at a cost that was economically viable."

PGS attributed a rise in fourth-quarter revenues to $118 million compared with $95 million in the three-month 1995 period to improved vessel productivity and expanded capacity, combined with significant increases in three-dimensional (3D) seismic data sales.
Revenues from the company's other activites during the period declined as a result of specific and significant software and processing system sales in 1995, which did not recur in 1996.

"The company periodically sells these systems and expects to do so in the future. However, the timing of such sales is difficult to predict and will result in varying trends among other revenues," the statement said.

It added that as a result of its evaluation of the current and expected market for marine seismic data it had ordered two additional Ramform vessels to be delivered in the first half 1998 at a cost of around $160 million.
"Additionally, the company is bidding on certain projects that, if awarded, may result in the company entering the floating production, storage and off-loading (FPSO) business," it said.
The estimated cost of a typical FPSO system, which would include a Ramform vessel, would cost between $180-$200 million.
